lines.japanese: えーと、まー、どーでもいいことなんですけどー。
lines.english: Uhhh, well, not that it matters, but...

lines.japanese: 色褪せない名曲、なーんて表現があるじゃないですか。でも逆に、色褪せているからこそ意味があるっていう音楽もあると思うんですよね。
lines.english: You know the phrase “a timeless classic”? Well, I think some music matters precisely because it shows its age.

lines.japanese: たとえば一例としてですけど。えー、さかのぼること十数年前、わが国におけるお茶の間的シーンにおいて、歌謡曲からニューミュージックへの過渡期に生まれた時代の寵児とも言える楽曲群があります。
lines.english: Take this example. Uh, a little over a decade ago, as popular music in Japan's living rooms made the transition from traditional pop to New Music, a group of songs appeared that could rightly be called the darlings of their era.

lines.japanese: ジャンル的にはアイドルポップなんて言うんですかね。まあ、これが世間の音楽通からは軽視されてると言いますか、同じ音楽というカテゴリーにすら組みこませてもらっていないフシがありますけども。
lines.english: I suppose you'd call the genre idol pop. Now, the music connoisseurs of the world tend to look down on it—or, in some cases, refuse to admit it into the category of music at all.

lines.japanese: ええまあ、たしかにアイドルソングっていうのは、当時からしてすでにショウビジネスのもっともエグい一面でして。百人の玄人に顔をしかめられようと、千人の素人に金を出させればええんじゃいな世界ですよね。
lines.english: And yes, idol songs were already the ugliest face of show business back then. Who cared if a hundred experts cringed, so long as a thousand amateurs coughed up their money?

lines.japanese: そもそもコマーシャルな素材としてたまたま音楽って手段を用いただけですから、アート的な意味での完成度なんて求められてませんし、あからさまに「作品であるより商品たれ」だったんですよ。
lines.english: Music just happened to be the medium chosen for a commercial venture in the first place. Nobody was asking for artistic excellence. The guiding principle was openly “Be a product, not a work of art.”

lines.japanese: でもね、ほら。そこまで貪欲に商業主義を前面に出しちゃってる曲がヒットチャートを独占したり大量生産されたりっていうのは、あの時代ならではの風潮でしょ。
lines.english: But, see, songs that flaunted commercial greed to that extent monopolizing the charts and rolling off the production line—that was very much a sign of those times.

lines.japanese: 現在だったらもっと上手いこと「作品」に昇華して見せたげないと、なかなかランキングの上位は取れないですよね。ましてやチャートにずらり並んだりなんて、とてもとても。
lines.english: These days, you won't get very high in the rankings unless you do a better job of dressing your product up as “art.” Let alone fill the charts with it. Oh, no.

lines.japanese: そんなアイドルポップ華やかなりし時代、あまたの少年少女たちが彗星のごとく現れては消えていったわけですが、えー、その中でもっとも知られているのが伝説の５人組『フリッキー５』ではないでしょうか。
lines.english: In that golden age of idol pop, countless boys and girls appeared and vanished like comets. Uh, surely the most famous of them were the legendary five-man group, Flicky 5.

lines.japanese: とくに国内シングルチャート１２週連続１位という偉業を成しとげた大ヒットナンバー『ほほえみジェノサイド』は、老若男女を問わず日本列島を熱狂の渦に巻きこんだものです。
lines.english: Their smash hit “Smiling Genocide,” in particular, achieved the remarkable feat of topping Japan's singles chart for twelve straight weeks, sweeping young and old alike into a frenzy across the nation.

lines.japanese: まだ四隅が丸かったころの画面の中で、彼らはステージ上に立ちこめた乳白色のミルキーウェイを切り、ピーターパンのように滑走していました。
lines.english: On screens whose four corners were still rounded, they cut through the milky-white Milky Way swirling over the stage, gliding like Peter Pan.

lines.japanese: ビブラートもヒーカップもどこ吹く風、あくまで自然体で歌いあげるナチュラルなスタイルは若さと瑞々しさに溢れていて、いっそ清々しいとさえ言えましょう。
lines.english: Vibrato? Vocal hiccups? They paid them no mind. Their natural, unforced style of singing brimmed with youth and freshness—bracing, one might even say.

lines.japanese: 歌は技術でなく心で歌うもの──だとすれば、パワーまかせのヴォーカルはティーンならではの爽快な情熱をプレーンなままに出力しており、聴く者のハートになにか勇気にも似たものを湧出させます。
lines.english: Songs are sung with the heart, not technique. If that is so, their full-power vocals gave unfiltered expression to the exhilarating passion of youth, stirring something akin to courage in the listener's heart.

lines.japanese: いま。いまだからこそ、聞いてもらいたい一曲。あの弾けたイントロが耳に飛びこんでくれば、銀色のきらびやかなステージ衣装をまとったフリファと共に、オーディエンスそれぞれの青春もまた甦るはず。
lines.english: Now. Now, of all times, this is a song I want you to hear. As that exuberant intro bursts into your ears, F5 will return in their glittering silver stage costumes—and every member of the audience's youth will return with them.

lines.japanese: 彼らの楽曲は、色褪せているからこそに美しい──そうです。伝説の少年たちが本邦音楽史に残した十代の叫びは、すなわち現代のミュージックシーンに欠けているなにかでもあるのです。
lines.english: Their songs are beautiful precisely because they show their age. Yes. The teenage cry those legendary boys left in our nation's musical history is also something missing from today's music scene.

lines.japanese: いやあ、アイドルって本当にいいものですね。
lines.english: Ah, idols really are wonderful things.

lines.japanese: 米田編集の眼球が追っていたのは、非情なことにそのあたりの行まででした。
lines.english: Cruelly enough, that was about as far as Editor Yoneda's eyes followed the text.

lines.japanese: 「はーい、それじゃー玉稿いただきましたー」
lines.english: “Okayyy, your deathless prose is officially received.”

lines.japanese: 「えええっ！」
lines.english: “Whaaat?!”

lines.japanese: 彼女がその原稿用紙五枚を早々と山折りして息つくように顔を上げるものですから、俺は思わず首から上を前に突きだすオーバーリアクションを披露してしまいました。
lines.english: She promptly folded the five sheets of manuscript paper in half, then looked up with a sigh. Before I knew it, I'd stuck everything from the neck up forward in a gigantic overreaction.

lines.japanese: 「え、もう読んだんすか？　読んでないすよね？　読めないほどひどいんすか！　ひどいんすか俺！」
lines.english: “Huh? You read it already? You didn't read it, did you? Is it too awful to read?! Am I that awful?!”

lines.japanese: 「違う違う、君を信頼してるからだってば」
lines.english: “No, no. It's because I trust you.”

lines.japanese: 「信頼……ああそう、それ！　信頼！　うん、信頼してるからこそ、もういいかなって」
lines.english: “Trust... Oh, right, that! Trust! Yes, I trust you, so I figured that was enough.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは右手をひらひらさせてソッポ向きながら、なんとも嘘くさい言葉をあさっての方向へ発射しました。
lines.english: Waving her right hand and turning away, Yuu launched those incredibly unconvincing words somewhere off in the wrong direction.

lines.japanese: 「いんすか！　いんすか、そんなんで！　いくらモノクロページの隅っこコラムだからって！　いくらアルバイトの素人に書かせた、誌面稼ぎのやっつけ仕事だからって！」
lines.english: “Is that okay?! Is that really okay?! Just because it's a little column tucked away on a black-and-white page?! Just because you got an amateur temp to slap it together to fill space?!”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　もう千歳君、自虐的だなあ。図々しいぐらいの自信がなきゃ、バイトとは言えこういう仕事やってけないよ」
lines.english: “What? Oh, Shuusuke, you're so hard on yourself. You need almost shameless confidence to survive this kind of work, even part-time.”

lines.japanese: 「俺に自信がないなら、米田さんには愛がないですよ！　担当さんとしての愛がなさすぎですよ！」
lines.english: “If I lack confidence, you lack love! You don't love me nearly enough as my editor!”

lines.japanese: 「だーいじょぶ、だってば。愛を込めて校正屋さんに回しとくから」
lines.english: “It'll be fiiine. I'll send it to the proofreader with love.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとまかせの愛！？」
lines.english: “Outsourced love?!”

lines.japanese: しかし俺の抗議もむなしく、米田さんは原稿用紙をＡ４封筒に入れると、その表面にでかでかと黒マジックで『懐レビュ』『１月売り』と殴り書きして、散らかったデスクの端に寄せました。
lines.english: My protests were in vain. Yuu slid the manuscript into an A4 envelope, scrawled “Nostalgia Review” and “On Sale in January” across it in big black marker, then pushed it to the edge of her messy desk.

lines.japanese: 「ええー、米田さぁーん。だって校正さんが見てくれるのは文字的なミスだけでしょー。文章の内容とかはチェックしなくていいんすかー」
lines.english: “Awww, Yuu. The proofreader only checks typos and stuff, right? Don't you need to check what it actually says?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、分かったよ……じゃあ、あとで読んどくから」
lines.english: “Hmm, all right... I'll read it later, then.”

lines.japanese: 「『じゃああとで』ってアナタ！　そんな、夏休みの宿題をいなす７月下旬の小学生みたいに！」
lines.english: “‘Later, then’?! Listen to yourself! You sound like a grade-schooler putting off summer homework in late July!”

lines.japanese: 「だって私、ここんとこ睡眠不足が続いててさぁ。働く大人はつらいわぁ……」
lines.english: “But I haven't been getting enough sleep lately. Being a working adult is sooo hard...”

lines.japanese: そんなことを言いながら、しょぼしょぼと子供みたいに目をこする米田さん。
lines.english: As she said it, Yuu rubbed her bleary eyes like a child.

lines.japanese: 「テンパってるときに千歳君の原稿読んでると、こっちまで洗脳されそうになっちゃうんだよねー」
lines.english: “When I'm frazzled, reading your stuff makes me feel like I'm about to get brainwashed too.”

lines.japanese: 「は、なんすか洗脳って」
lines.english: “Huh? What's this about brainwashing?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら。千歳君、それらしい御託ならべてなんでもかんでも誉めちぎるじゃない。だからうっかり、あーそうかもなー、これはこれでいいのかもなーとかってさ」
lines.english: “You know. You reel off all these plausible-sounding arguments and praise anything and everything to the skies. Before I know it, I'm thinking, ‘Oh, maybe he's right. Maybe this is good in its own way.’”

lines.japanese: 「それ洗脳じゃないっすよ！　啓蒙っすよ！」
lines.english: “That's not brainwashing! That's enlightenment!”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、ほんと、フリッキー５はイイっすよ？　アリっすよ？　捨てたもんじゃないっすよ？」
lines.english: “I mean, seriously, Flicky 5 are good! They work! They're nothing to sneeze at!”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい、あとで読むからいいってば……まあ、うら若き乙女のころは私も人並にハマったけどさ」
lines.english: “Yes, yes. I'll read it later, so enough already... Well, I was as crazy about them as anyone in my tender maiden years.”

lines.japanese: 「え、誰のファンだったんすか？　やっぱホソリュー？　それとも渋いとこ突いてマサシとか？」
lines.english: “Oh, whose fan were you? Hosoryuu, of course? Or did you go for a less obvious choice, like Masashi?”

lines.japanese: 「うあー、やめてやめて。数々の若気のいたりが甦る」
lines.english: “Ugh, stop, stop. All the stupid things I did in my youth are coming back.”

lines.japanese: 「甦らせてくださいよぅ。フリッキー５は時空を越えるレジェンドっすよ。いっそ巻頭特集でどどんと一発やりましょうよ、フリファ・メモリアルとかって」
lines.english: “Let them! Flicky 5 are legends beyond time and space. Let's go all out and make them the lead feature. A big F5 Memorial or something.”

lines.japanese: 「しつこいなー。キミ、フリーター辞めてうちの営業部入ったら？」
lines.english: “You don't give up, do you? Why don't you quit drifting between jobs and join our sales department?”

lines.japanese: 「一流企業に縁故採用！？　マジっすか、入ります入ります、紹介状ください紹介状」
lines.english: “A personal connection gets me into a top company?! Seriously? I'm in, I'm in! Write me a recommendation! A recommendation!”

lines.japanese: 「ヒラの私になに期待するかな、この子は。だいたいさ、千歳君まだ就職する気なんてないんでしょ？　いいよねえ、青い春って。手探りの季節だァ、可能性の塊だァ」
lines.english: “What are you expecting from a lowly employee like me? Besides, you don't even want a permanent job yet, do you? Ah, youth. Must be nice. A season of finding your way! A great lump of potential!”

lines.japanese: 「痛っ、痛っ！　オフィス・レディの疲弊した眼光がプーの柔肌にひしひし痛いっす！」
lines.english: “Ow, ow! A worn-out working woman's glare stings my tender, unemployed skin!”

lines.japanese: とかっておどけてはみせても、やっぱり十も離れてない米田さんにまるでモラトリアム世代の象徴みたいな目で見られると、なんだか申しわけない気分になってきます。
lines.english: I played the fool, but when Yuu—who wasn't even ten years older than me—looked at me like I embodied a whole generation putting off adulthood, I did feel a little guilty.

lines.japanese: 一流大学をストレートで出てそのまま大手出版社に入ったという米田さんは、体を俺に向けたままで、ちらりとパソコンのディスプレイを確認しました。
lines.english: Yuu had gone straight through a top university and into a major publisher. Still facing me, she glanced at her computer screen.

lines.japanese: 「んー、やっぱ違うかな……」
lines.english: “Hmm, no, that's not it...”

lines.japanese: そして、小さな声でつぶやいてからマウスに手を伸ばしました。
lines.english: Murmuring to herself, she reached for the mouse.

lines.japanese: 「旋回やり過ぎたか……端だけバンクさせて……うーん、いっそここは原形とどめないぐらいに……」
lines.english: “Too much twist... Just bank the edges... Hmm, maybe I should warp it out of all recognition...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんの右手の下からカチカチ音がするたびに、画面の中の見出し文字がうねったり尖ったりその表情を変えていきます。
lines.english: Every click from beneath her right hand changed the expression of the headline on the screen, making it curve or sprout sharp points.
“Ooh? Ooh?”

lines.japanese: 指一本で出来るマジック。同じ文字列でもほんの少しの加工でいろんな印象になるものです。
lines.english: Magic with one finger. A tiny bit of manipulation could give the same string of letters all sorts of different impressions.

lines.japanese: 「はー。なんか便利っすねえ、こんぴーたー」
lines.english: “Wow. These compooters are pretty handy, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　ああ……」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんはいまどき珍しい日本語に遭遇したかのような目で、ぼけーっと突っ立っていた俺の姿を見上げました。
lines.english: She looked up at me standing there in a daze, as if I'd used an expression you hardly heard anymore.

lines.japanese: 「うん、便利っていうかもう必需品だよね。いまだいぶ安くなってきてるし、千歳君も早く揃えた方がいいよ。そうすれば私ももっと仕事振れるし」
lines.english: “Yeah, they're not just handy. They're essential now. Prices have come down a lot, too. You should get one soon, Shuusuke. Then I could give you more work.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、でもその前に、キミには携帯電話を持ってほしいんだけど──」
lines.english: “But before that, I'd really like you to get a cell phone—”

lines.japanese: 「──っと！　ちょっと待って、内線だ」
lines.english: “—Oh! Hang on, it's an internal call.”

lines.japanese: 林檎マークの箱型機械の横で、クリーム色の電話機がプルプル鳴りだしました。米田さんは俺にてのひらを向けながら、もう片方の手で受話器を取りあげます。
lines.english: Beside the box-shaped machine with the apple logo, a cream-colored telephone began to ring. Holding one palm toward me, Yuu picked up the receiver with her other hand.

lines.japanese: 「へい米田っす……はい……あー、はいどーも、替わりますー」
lines.english: “Yep, Yoneda here... Yes... Oh, right, thanks. I'll take it.”

lines.japanese: 「もしもし！　ハイっ、ご無沙汰しておりますヨネダです！　いえっ、こちらこそお世話になっております」
lines.english: “Hello! Yes, it's Yoneda! It's been a while! No, thank you, it's always a pleasure working with you.”

lines.japanese: ひと懐っこい声で応対しながら、米田編集は無意識なのかその場でぺこぺこ頭を下げはじめました。
lines.english: As she answered in that friendly voice, Editor Yoneda started bowing on the spot, apparently without realizing it.

lines.japanese: ふと周りを見れば、メンズフリーズ編集部は入稿日が近いのか、皆さん忙しなく動きまわったり一心にキーボードを叩いたりしていました。
lines.english: Looking around, I noticed everyone in the Men's Freeze editorial office either rushing about or hammering away at their keyboards. The print deadline must be close.

lines.japanese: 電話の声やＯＡ機器の音が雑然としたオフィスに満ちていて、ある種の緊迫した空気が漂っています。
lines.english: Telephone voices and office machines filled the cluttered room, and a certain tension hung in the air.

lines.japanese: 隣りの机で探しものをしている男性編集者の苛立たしさが、なんだか無職の俺に帰れと言ってるように思えてきました。
lines.english: An irritated male editor looking for something at the next desk made me feel as if he was telling my unemployed self to go home.

lines.japanese: あー、なんか居づらい空気。苦手だなあ、こういうの……。
lines.english: Ahhh, hard to feel comfortable here. I'm no good with this kind of atmosphere...

lines.japanese: 「ごめんごめん。えーと、なんの話だったっけ？」
lines.english: “Sorry, sorry. Uh, what were we talking about?”

lines.japanese: 一歩あとずさりかけたところで、受話器を置いた米田さんが、椅子を回して俺に向きなおりました。
lines.english: Just as I was about to take a step back, Yuu put down the receiver and swiveled her chair around to face me.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうそう！　千歳君にもっと仕事頼みたいって話だ。どう、いまちょうど一本あるんだけど、引きうけてくれない？」
lines.english: “Oh, right! Giving you more work. Well? I have something right now, actually. Want to take it?”

lines.japanese: 「は。マジっすか」
lines.english: “Huh. Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 居心地の悪さになんとなく背中が丸くなってきた俺ですが、仕事の話となれば堂々と胸を張れます。
lines.english: The awkward atmosphere had begun to make me hunch over, but talk of work let me puff out my chest with pride.

lines.japanese: 「うん。それでお金貯めて、早くケータイ買ってね」
lines.english: “Yep. Save up and buy a cell phone soon.”

lines.japanese: 「で、で、どんなお仕事なんすか」
lines.english: “So, so, what's the job?”

lines.japanese: 俺は話を逸らして詰めよりました。
lines.english: I changed the subject and leaned in.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、ちょっと待ってね……」
lines.english: “Uh, hang on...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは事務机に積もった書類や資料の山に手を突っこみ、その中から一冊のハードカバーを引きぬきました。
lines.english: Yuu plunged a hand into the mountain of papers and reference material on her desk and pulled out a hardcover book.

lines.japanese: 「とりあえず、これあげる。ちょっと前に下が出したものなんだけど」
lines.english: “Here, you can have this for now. Downstairs put it out a little while ago.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは本を持っていない方の手で床を指差しました。たしか下のフロアには文芸誌や一般書籍の編集部なんかがあったはずです。
lines.english: With her free hand, she pointed at the floor. If I remembered right, the literary magazine and general book departments were on the floor below.

lines.japanese: 「どうかな。来月頭ぐらいまでに、これの紹介文５０００文字。かなりユルめの文体で」
lines.english: “How about it? Five thousand characters introducing this, by the start of next month or so. In a pretty loose style.”

lines.japanese: 俺は首を大袈裟に傾けて、米田さんの持っている本を横から覗きこみました。そして、それほど厚くないことだけ確認するとその場で即断しました。
lines.english: I tilted my head extravagantly and peered sideways at the book in her hand. Having checked only that it wasn't very thick, I made up my mind on the spot.

lines.japanese: 「ようがす。引きうけましょう」
lines.english: “Very good. I shall accept.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん。また適当に誉めちぎっといて」
lines.english: “Good, good. Just praise it to the skies again.”

lines.japanese: 「誉め一丁、喜んで！」
lines.english: “One order of praise, coming right up!”

lines.japanese: 米田さんが差しだした本を、俺は卒業証書を受けとるみたいに両手で丁重に受けとりました。
lines.english: I respectfully received the book with both hands, as if she were presenting my diploma.

lines.japanese: 「……で、どんな内容なんすかこれ」
lines.english: “...So, what's it about?”

lines.japanese: 「元ＡＶ嬢の実体験エッセイ集」
lines.english: “A collection of personal essays by a former porn actress.”

lines.japanese: 「ぅわお！　服脱ぐ女優が心まで脱ぎました！」
lines.english: “Wow! An actress who bares her body bares her soul!”

lines.japanese: 「聞いた話だと、基本えっち系なんだけど、ときおり泣きどころもあるらしいよ」
lines.english: “From what I've heard, it's mostly sexy stuff, but there are a few tearjerkers here and there.”

lines.japanese: 「ポロリもあるけどホロリもあるよ！」
lines.english: “An eyeful—and an eye full of tears!”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、そんな感じの馬鹿テキストでお願い」
lines.english: “Exactly. That kind of stupid copy, please.”

lines.japanese: 「……いま、馬鹿って言いました？」
lines.english: “...Did you just say ‘stupid’?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、早い話がコレ、うちの商品の販促だから。いつもの調子で、ベタベタに甘やかしたレビューお願いしますね、千歳先生」
lines.english: “Well, basically, it's promotion for one of our products. So I'd like your usual sickly-sweet, indulgent review, Mr. Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いま馬鹿って言いましたよね？　千歳先生に」
lines.english: “No, you just called Mr. Chitose stupid, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「それにしてもカケル遅いねえ。自分から来るって言ったんでしょ？」
lines.english: “Kakeru sure is late. He's the one who said he was coming, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ふんだ、そんな、思いだしたように話題変えたって釣られないやい」
lines.english: “Hmph. Don't think I'll take the bait just because you changed the subject like you suddenly remembered it.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、あの子が時間守らないのはいまに始まったことでもないか」
lines.english: “Well, it's hardly news that he can't be on time.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは椅子をきぃと軋ませて、背もたれに体重を預けました。
lines.english: Yuu leaned back, making her chair squeak.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、カケルってさ、昔からああだったの？」
lines.english: “Hey, has Kakeru always been like that?”

lines.japanese: 「え、話変えるの癪ですけど、なんすか『ああ』って」
lines.english: “Huh? I resent the change of subject, but what do you mean, ‘like that’?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、ああいうさ……うーん、マイペースっていうか、自分を貫くっていうか……」
lines.english: “You know, like... Hmm, going at his own pace, I guess. Or sticking to his guns...”

lines.japanese: 「ぶっちゃけて言うと？」
lines.english: “To put it bluntly?”

lines.japanese: 「クソ生意気なガキ」
lines.english: “A fucking smart-mouthed brat.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえさん、ぶっちゃけ過ぎ」
lines.english: “Whoa, that’s a little too blunt.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いいんだけどね。私は仕事柄、エキセントリックな人間を相手にするのわりと慣れてるし。あと軽部先輩から紹介された時点で、いきなり『素行に問題あるが長い目で見守ってくれ』なんて言われてたし」
lines.english: “Well, it's fine. I'm fairly used to dealing with eccentric people in this job. And when Karube introduced him, he told me straight off, ‘His behavior's a problem, but give him time and look out for him.’”

lines.japanese: 「でも、普通はそう簡単に済まされないでしょ。あんな生き方してて、ねえ、損じゃない」
lines.english: “But most people aren't going to let him off that easily. Living like that, I mean, he's only hurting himself.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ほら、あれっすよ。きっと彼、フクザツな生い立ちとかあるんすよ」
lines.english: “Ah, you know, it's probably that thing. A troubled childhood or something.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、グレ方としちゃ中途半端だと思うけどね。はっきり言って大人げないし。構ってほしくて憎まれ口叩いてる子供みたいじゃない？」
lines.english: “Hmm, it's pretty half-assed as rebellion goes. Frankly, he's immature. Doesn't he seem like a kid saying nasty things because he wants attention?”

lines.japanese: 「ええまあ。そう見えるからこそ、べつに腹も立たないんすけど」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. That's exactly why it doesn't really make me mad.”

lines.japanese: 「まあねえ……昔の軽部先輩みたいに、何十人っていうヤンキー集団のアタマ張っちゃうような本気っぽいのも、それはそれでドン引きだけどさ」
lines.english: “I guess... Though the serious kind, like Karube back in the day, leading a gang of dozens of delinquents—that's a turnoff in its own way.”

lines.japanese: 「え、うそ！　低俗なお下劣ジョークを飛ばしては日々女性アルバイトにこっぴどく叱られている、あのうだつの上がらない軽部狩男３５歳に、そんな人知れぬバリバリ伝説が！？」
lines.english: “What? No way! Karuo Karube, age thirty-five, that hopeless guy who cracks filthy, lowbrow jokes and gets chewed out by the female part-timers every day—he has a secret hell-raising legend?!”

lines.japanese: 「え、初耳？　うっそ、先輩これ内緒にしてたのかな……あはは、いまの聞かなかったことにしてね」
lines.english: “Huh, you hadn't heard? Really? Maybe he was keeping it a secret... Ahaha, pretend you didn't hear that.”

lines.japanese: 「え、えええ、難しい記憶操作をさらりと要請するなあこのひと」
lines.english: “Wha—whaaat? This woman just casually requested some advanced memory manipulation.”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、じゃあ話をカケルに戻そう。千歳君は、彼と長いんだっけ？」
lines.english: “Uh, let's get back to Kakeru, then. You've known him a long time, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、初めて会ったのは一年ぐらい前すかね。たしか去年のいま頃だったかな、裸Ｙシャツ喫茶の立て看板を設置するバイトでたまたま同じ組になったんすよ」
lines.english: “Hmm, I first met him about a year ago. Around this time last year, I think. We happened to get paired up on a job putting out signs for a café with naked girls in dress shirts.”

lines.japanese: 「なんつーバイトしてんの、キミら」
lines.english: “What kind of jobs are you two doing?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、なに言ってんですか。ジャンル的にはある意味、広告代理業っすよ。つったらリクルートの花形、大学４年生の憧れじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Now, now, what are you saying? In a sense, the field is advertising. That's the star of the job market, the dream of every college senior.”

lines.japanese: 「で？　夜中にあちこちまわって？　電柱にタテカンくくりつけてるうちに意気投合して？」
lines.english: “So? You went around at night? And hit it off while tying those signs to utility poles?”

lines.japanese: 「や、そうでもなかったすよ。俺はぺらぺら喋ってたけど、彼はむっつり黙ってたし。むしろウザがられてたんじゃないかなあ」
lines.english: “No, not really. I babbled on, but he stayed sullen and quiet. If anything, I think I was getting on his nerves.”

lines.japanese: 「だよねえ。あの子、そんな人なつっこくないもんねえ」
lines.english: “Yeah, that figures. He's not exactly friendly.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、まあ。ただ、そんときカケルくんが何気に教えてくれた洋食屋があって、試しに行ってみたらいいカンジだったんです」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. But Kakeru happened to mention a Western-style restaurant, so I tried it out and liked the place.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それがアレキサンダー？」
lines.english: “Oh, that was Alexander?”

lines.japanese: 「そです。ほいで、通ってるうちに何度か遭遇して」
lines.english: “Yep. Then I kept going and ran into him a few times.”

lines.japanese: 「で、自然と意気投合してった、ってわけだ」
lines.english: “And you naturally hit it off.”

lines.japanese: 「や、べつに」
lines.english: “No, not particularly.”

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃいつ意気投合すんの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Then when do you hit it off?”

lines.japanese: 「え、この話は意気投合オチにしなきゃいけないんですか」
lines.english: “Huh? Does this story have to end with us hitting it off?”

lines.japanese: 「私、若さゆえに不器用な男同士が握手する瞬間って好きなのよねー」
lines.english: “I love that moment when two guys who are awkward because they're young finally shake hands.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。そいじゃ近日中に意気投合しときます」
lines.english: “Right. Well, we'll hit it off sometime soon, then.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、キミら、まだしてなかったの？」
lines.english: “What? You two haven't done it yet?”

lines.japanese: 「ねえさん、その言い方なんか薔薇色」
lines.english: “Uh, you’re making this sound a little gay.”

lines.japanese: 「カケルってさ、好きな子とかいないのかな」
lines.english: “I wonder if Kakeru has a girl he likes.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっと、この流れでコイバナに持ってくんすか。べつにうちら、薔薇色の関係ないすよ」
lines.english: “Wait, you're turning this into love talk now? There's nothing gay going on between us.”

lines.japanese: 「そうじゃなくてさ、あいつも真面目に恋愛なんかすれば角が取れて丸くなるんじゃないかなーって」
lines.english: “No, I mean, maybe a serious relationship would smooth out his rough edges a little.”

lines.japanese: 「……ん？　それとも？　真面目な恋に破れてトゲが出たとか？」
lines.english: “...Hmm? Or did he get those thorns from a serious heartbreak?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、なんにしても、あの圭角の多さと言うか、切れ味鋭いエッジこそがカケルくんの持ち味じゃないかと思いますが」
lines.english: “Well, whatever the case, I think all those sharp corners, that razor edge, are exactly what makes Kakeru Kakeru.”

lines.japanese: 「鋭すぎでしょ。千歳君、カケルのスレッドとか見たことある？」
lines.english: “Too sharp. Have you ever seen the threads about him?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんすかそれ」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか……パソコン持ってないのか……」
lines.english: “Oh, right... You don't have a computer...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは眠たげな声で答えながら、ねむねむとまぶたのマッサージを始めました。どうやらけっこうお疲れで、ちょっと気を抜くと睡魔がやってくるみたいです。
lines.english: Answering in a sleepy voice, Yuu began drowsily massaging her eyelids. She seemed pretty tired; sleep was ready to pounce the moment she let her guard down.

lines.japanese: 「いやねー、要するに、ネットで鳳凰寺カケルを悪く言ってる連中ってのが結構いてさー」
lines.english: “Well, basically, there's a fair number of people bad-mouthing Kakeru Hououji online.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「そう驚くことでもないでしょ。カケルって現場でもああだから、良く思ってない関係者なんて星の数ほどいるだろうし、プライベートじゃなおさら、ねえ？」
lines.english: “It's hardly a shock. He's like that on the job too, so there must be more people in the industry who dislike him than there are stars in the sky. And in his private life, well, even more, right?”

lines.japanese: 「や、ていうか、インターネットってそんななんすか」
lines.english: “No, I mean, is that what the Internet's like?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、漠然とした質問だね。そんなと言えばそんなだよ」
lines.english: “Hmm, that's a pretty vague question. Well, yes, I guess it is like that.”

lines.japanese: 「うそーん、カルチャーショック。いやだわあ電脳社会」
lines.english: “No waaay. Culture shock. This cyber-society is awful.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう一面もあるって話だよ。後学のためにも、ネットカフェとか行って見てみれば？」
lines.english: “I'm saying that's one side of it. Why don't you go look in an Internet café? For future reference.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、やだ恐ーい、そんな見えない悪意の吹きだまりー。わたしダメなの、ひとの悪口とか言うのも聞くのも苦手なのー」
lines.english: “Ohhh, no, I'm scared! All that invisible malice collecting in one place! I just can't, darling. I hate saying mean things about people or hearing them.”

lines.japanese: 俺がてのひらを頬に当ててくねくねしているうちに、米田さんはまたマウスをカチカチさせていました。
lines.english: While I pressed my palms to my cheeks and wriggled, Yuu was clicking her mouse again.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、こことか。雑誌の読者モデルとか追っかけてる娘たちが集まるサイトなんだけど、カケルってあのルックスでしょ、良くも悪くもその手の娘たちにチェックされやすいんだぁ」
lines.english: “Here, this site. It's where girls who follow magazine reader-models hang out. You know what Kakeru looks like. For better or worse, girls like that tend to keep an eye on him.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そっか、カケルくんたまに著者近影みたいな感じで顔出ししてますもんね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. He does show his face sometimes, like an author photo.”

lines.japanese: 「アレ、本人イヤがってるけどね。『いや俺はどうでもいいけどヨネに迷惑かかるかもよ』とか何とか言っちゃってさ。なーに迷惑って、おまえは指名手配でもされてんのか！　あはは！」
lines.english: “He hates that, though. Says things like, ‘I don't care, but it might cause trouble for Yone.’ What trouble? Are you wanted by the police?! Ahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、そんで？　これは何なんすか？」
lines.english: “Right, and? What's this?”

lines.japanese: 俺は米田さんの隣りに並んで、ディスプレイを覗きこんでみました。細かい文字の並んだ画面が、彼女の操作で下へ下へと流れていきます。
lines.english: I stood beside Yuu and peered at the display. Under her control, the screen full of tiny text scrolled down and down.

lines.japanese: 「あのね、ここのＢＢＳはとくにカケルのアンチが多いの。笑っちゃうのが、たまに自称関係者だの自称元カノだの自称ナンパされただのが出没して──」
lines.english: “See, this board's especially full of Kakeru-haters. The funny thing is, people occasionally show up claiming to know him, or be his ex-girlfriend, or have been hit on by him—”

lines.japanese: 「自称に優しい自称天国だ」
lines.english: “A paradise for the self-proclaimed. Self-proclaim away!”

lines.japanese: 「要は覆面座談会だからね、言ったもん勝ちだよ。わりと本物っぽいのが紛れてたりもするんだけど──」
lines.english: “Basically, it's an anonymous roundtable. Whoever says it wins. Some of them seem pretty genuine, though—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、この辺おもしろいよ。鳳凰寺カケル名言集。みんな、カケルのキャラよく掴んでるんだこれが」
lines.english: “—Oh, this bit's funny. ‘Great Sayings of Kakeru Hououji.’ They really have his personality down.”

lines.japanese: 「え、読んで読んで」
lines.english: “Oh, read it, read it.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、じゃあこの辺から……」
lines.english: “Hmm, starting here, then...”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは咳払いひとつしてから、カケルくんの声色と口調を真似て読みはじめました。
lines.english: After clearing her throat, Yuu began to read, mimicking Kakeru's voice and manner of speaking.

lines.japanese: 「『まあ、どんな容姿でも自信を持つことは大事だよね』」
lines.english: “‘Well, confidence matters, no matter what you look like.’”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、言いそぉ……」
lines.english: “Ugh, I can hear him saying that...”

lines.japanese: 「『ごめん、チョコは好きだけど君は嫌いだから』」
lines.english: “‘Sorry, I like chocolate, but I don't like you.’”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、ホントっぽくて夢に見そぉ……」
lines.english: “Ugh, sounds so real I'll have nightmares...”

lines.japanese: 「『死ねよ、腐れマ××』」
lines.english: “‘Die, you rotten p**sy.’”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、それも言いそうだぁ……ていうか、あああ、昨日聞いちゃったあああ」
lines.english: “Ugh, he'd say that too... Wait, aaah, I heard him say that yesterdayyy!”

lines.japanese: 「『あァ？　それ、俺の子だって証拠あんのかよ』」
lines.english: “‘Huh? You got any proof that kid's mine?’”

lines.japanese: 「はは、それはまさか……いや、ビミョーか……絶対ないとも……」
lines.english: “Haha, surely not that... No, it's a little iffy... Can't say absolutely not...”

lines.japanese: 「『でも、そのひと最後は自分から腰振ってましたよ検事さん』」
lines.english: “‘But she started doing the thrusting herself by the end, Mr. Prosecutor.’”

lines.japanese: 「ａｔ法廷！？」
lines.english: “In a courtroom?!”

lines.japanese: 「──まだまだあるけど、続ける？」
lines.english: “—There's plenty more. Want me to go on?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、結構です……ぽんぽん痛くなってきました……あたたた」
lines.english: “No, thank you... My tummy's starting to hurt... Ow, ow, ow.”

lines.japanese: 「あとね、街で見かけた鳳凰寺カケル、なんてスレもあって」
lines.english: “And there's a thread called ‘Kakeru Hououji Sightings Around Town.’”

lines.japanese: 「や、もういいですって」
lines.english: “No, I said that's enough.”

lines.japanese: 「深夜の雑木林からスコップ担いで出てきたとか、冬の波止場で人相の悪い男たちと中国語で密談していたとか、難病と闘う少年にホームランの約束をして勇気を与えていたとか」
lines.english: “He was coming out of the woods late at night with a shovel over his shoulder, or secretly meeting shifty-looking men on a winter wharf and speaking Chinese, or giving courage to a boy battling a serious illness by promising him a home run.”

lines.japanese: 「も、ぜんぜん『街で』見かけてないじゃないすか。美談まぎれてるし」
lines.english: “None of that's ‘around town’ anymore. And there's a heartwarming story mixed in.”

lines.japanese: 「で実際カケルって、交遊関係どうなの？　なんか、ガラの悪い連中と一緒にいました系のタレコミ多いんだけど」
lines.english: “So what's his social circle actually like? There are lots of reports of the ‘he was with some rough-looking guys’ variety.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そうなんすか？」
lines.english: “Huh, really?”

lines.japanese: 「あの子、いまはまだ写真週刊誌のネタになるほどの知名度ないけどさ。正直これからガンガン前に出ていける逸材だと思うんだよね。本人も作品もそういうオーラ出てるし」
lines.english: “He isn't famous enough for the photo tabloids to bother with him yet. But honestly, I think he has what it takes to really make it big. Both he and his work have that aura.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、あとはカケル自身がその辺マジメに考えてるかどうかなんだけど。私生活含めて」
lines.english: “So the rest depends on whether he takes that stuff seriously himself. His private life included.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、言っときますけど俺、カケルくんの私生活なんて知りませんよ。うちら暗黙の了解で、お互いのプライバシーに深く突っこまないすから」
lines.english: “Oh, just so you know, I don't know anything about his private life. We have an unspoken agreement not to dig too deeply into each other's personal business.”

lines.japanese: 「なーんだ。キミら若いくせして、都会のマンションみたいな付き合いしてんだね」
lines.english: “Oh. You two are young, but you get along like neighbors in a city apartment building.”

lines.japanese: 「そそそ。こうね、深過ぎず浅過ぎずーぐらいが一番なんすよ、人間と人間は」
lines.english: “Exactly. Not too deep, not too shallow—that's best, you know, between one person and another.”

lines.japanese: 「はは～ん？　それは分かるけど、口に出来ちゃうのが若さよねえ鷲介クン？」
lines.english: “Ah-hah? I get that, but being able to say it out loud is what makes you young, Shuusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いまの発言、青かったすか」
lines.english: “Oh, did that sound immature?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとねー。そんなことくれー、言われなくても大人はみんな知ってるのよ～ん♪」
lines.english: “A little. All the grown-ups know that much without being told, sweetie. ♪”

lines.japanese: 「ぅわお！　大人かっけぇー！」
lines.english: “Wow! Grown-ups are so cool!”

lines.japanese: 「ああッ！　米田ァ、てめえこれ、また間違ってるじゃねえか！」
lines.english: “Hey! Yoneda, goddammit, you've screwed this up again!”

lines.japanese: 呑気な雑談に花を咲かせていると、とつぜん島端のお誕生席から悲鳴のような怒声が投げはなたれました。
lines.english: While we were enjoying our leisurely little chat, an angry yell, almost a shriek, suddenly shot over from the seat at the end of the desk cluster.

lines.japanese: 「マップとキャプション、一個ずつズレてる！　先月と同じ間違い！」
lines.english: “The maps and captions are all one place off! Same mistake as last month!”

lines.japanese: 青焼きの束を突きだし、それを残った手の甲でばしばし叩いてみせる壮年の編集者。米田さんは身を乗りだすように立ちあがりました。
lines.english: The middle-aged editor held out a bundle of blue proofs, smacking it with the back of his free hand. Yuu jumped up and leaned forward.

lines.japanese: 「うぞっ！？」
lines.english: “You’re kidding?!”

lines.japanese: 「なんで俺が嘘つくんだよ！」
lines.english: “Why the hell would I kid about that?!”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃあああ！　すいません至急修正します！」
lines.english: “Aaaargh! I'm sorry! I'll fix it right away!”

lines.japanese: 両手で頭を抱えています。お、大人つれぇー。
lines.english: Both hands clutched her head. G-grown-ups have it rough.

lines.japanese: 「えーと……それじゃ自分、そろそろ失礼しますね」
lines.english: “Uh... Well, I'd better be going.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あー、ごめんねえバタバタしちゃって。あはは、やーねーアイツ、ひとの細かいミスばっかり見つけちゃって。地図なんてちょっとぐらい間違えたって、ほっときゃ読者の方向音痴のせいになるのにねえ」
lines.english: “Oh, uh, sorry for all the rushing around. Ahaha, he's awful, isn't he? Always catching every little mistake I make. A slightly wrong map wouldn't matter. Leave it alone and they'd blame the readers' terrible sense of direction.”

lines.japanese: 「ないない、それはない」
lines.english: “No, no. That doesn't work.”

lines.japanese: 俺は最後にひとツッコミ入れてから、にこやかに頭を下げて出口へ向かいました。
lines.english: I got in one last comeback, then bowed with a smile and headed for the door.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、千歳君！　それじゃあ下の喫茶で時間潰しててよ。カケルのケータイに、そっちへ行くようメール入れとくから」
lines.english: “Oh, Shuusuke! Kill some time at the café downstairs. I'll email Kakeru's cell and tell him to meet you there.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それはどうも、お手数かけますー」
lines.english: “Oh, thanks. Sorry for the trouble.”

lines.japanese: もう一度おじぎして、その後はすみやかに編集部を去りました。
lines.english: I bowed once more, then promptly left the editorial office.

lines.japanese: 入稿前の忙しい時期に、ちょっと長居しすぎちゃいましたかね。でも、渡すものだけ渡して帰るのもまた素っ気ないし。
lines.english: Maybe I'd stayed a little too long at such a busy time before the print deadline. But handing over the manuscript and leaving right away would've been rather cold too.

lines.japanese: 引き際のタイミングって、いつでも難しいですよね？
lines.english: It's always hard to know when to leave, isn't it?
